title: Connections page (#2338)

chrome.from: http://localhost:3011/integrations (origin/main at 5681df51), signed in as the e2e test user, 2026-10-20

frames.title: A working connection open: Pennie Salesforce
A connection with a problem open: Achieve Salesforce
Add connection: saving, the login being checked
Add connection: an org Bidspoke does not know
Add connection: Google, a company mailbox or drive
Add connection: Google, your own account
Remove a connection no workflow uses
Login checks not answering: statuses as last known
The connections could not be loaded

decisions.decision: The page is a list on the left, grouped by service, and the chosen connection's details on the right.
decisions.why: Round 1: one place to see every connection and one to work on the chosen one.
decisions.check: The page holds a connection list and a detail panel, the list wholly to the left of the panel and the two side by side.

decisions.decision: Integrations is renamed Connections in the nav, with a plug icon, and the Slack alert login (Bidspoke Alerts) and the HTTP services are listed as connections.
decisions.why: Round 2: one page for every login Bidspoke holds.
decisions.check: The nav has a link reading Connections with a plug icon and none reading Integrations; where the list is drawn, Bidspoke Alerts sits under Slack and Lender API and Regal webhook under HTTP.

decisions.decision: A Needs attention group comes first, holding every connection with a problem, each with its service and what is wrong under its name; the rest are grouped by service, alphabetical.
decisions.why: Round 3: what is in trouble is read first.
decisions.check: The first group heading reads Needs attention and holds exactly the fixture's connections whose status is not ok, each with "<service>, <status, lower case>" under its name; the remaining headings are the other services in alphabetical order, each listing its working connections alphabetically.

decisions.decision: Section headings in the list are dark, normal case, 14px semibold, with a line above each section. This is for the Connections page only, not a rule for other lists.
decisions.check: Every group heading is coloured #1D212F, 14px, weight 600, not upper case, and every heading after the first has a line above it.

decisions.decision: The detail panel has three tabs: Connection, Used by (n), History.
decisions.check: The detail panel has a tablist of exactly three tabs reading Connection, Used by (<the connection's workflow count>) and History, with Connection selected.

decisions.decision: Reconnect and Replace are quiet buttons under the facts; Remove is set apart in its own row at the bottom of the panel.
decisions.why: Rounds 6 and 9c: the everyday actions together, the destructive one apart.
decisions.check: Below the facts a row of quiet buttons (neither blue nor red) reads Reconnect and Replace, or Replace alone when the problem notice holds Reconnect, and Remove is in a later row of its own, below them.

decisions.decision: A problem shows as a shaded notice at the top of the Connection tab: when it began and its cause, its effect, a grey fix line, and a blue Reconnect inside it; the status under the name reads in red.
decisions.why: Round 7, with the wording reworded so no line ends on a lone word.
decisions.check: The first thing under the tabs is a notice whose lines read "Since 9:52 AM ET, Salesforce has refused its client secret.", "Achieve report import stops at its Salesforce step." and a grey "Reconnect with a new client secret from Achieve's Salesforce admin.", holding a blue Reconnect button, and the status under the name reads Needs reconnecting in red.

decisions.decision: On the canvas, a step's Connection field is the app's dropdown with the chosen connection's name, with only "Acts as <who>" under it; nothing about status on a healthy day. A connection with a problem adds one red line, "Needs reconnecting on the Connections page", its last two words a dark underlined link to that page.
decisions.provenBy: docs/design/connections-step-form.html and its checks (connections-step-form.checks.js), which hold the step form frames

decisions.decision: While a workflow uses the connection, Remove is greyed out, its row reads "Cannot be removed while a workflow uses it.", and a plain "Used by:" list of the workflows sits under the row, with no button.
decisions.check: Remove is disabled and grey, its row reads "Cannot be removed while a workflow uses it.", and under it a "Used by:" list names every workflow using the connection as a dark underlined link, with no button in the list.

decisions.decision: Google mailboxes and drives: an entry at the top of the Google section; choosing it shows in the panel the heading, a sentence whose term "domain wide delegation" carries its one sentence explanation, one row per entry with address, kind, "Added by <who>, <date>" and Remove on one line, and an add box with Add.
decisions.why: Round 10, and Dan's decision of 2026-10-18 that any signed in user may add to the list.
decisions.check: Mailboxes and drives is the first entry under the Google heading and is chosen; the panel is headed Google mailboxes and drives, its term domain wide delegation can take focus and carries an explanation, it has one row per fixture entry reading address, kind, Added by <who>, <date> and Remove on a single line, and an input with an Add button.

decisions.decision: Add connection is the blue button at the top right of the page, always there once the list has loaded; it opens the form in the right panel in place of the details, with nothing chosen in the list.
decisions.check: A blue button reading Add connection sits at the top right of the page, level with the page title; on the add frames the right panel holds the form headed Add a connection and no list item is chosen.

decisions.decision: The service is chosen from a grid of tiles in two columns, each the service's name and one line of what it connects. The tiles come from the service catalogue, so a service appears once its catalogue entry ships.
decisions.why: Round 12, and Dan asked how a service is added.
decisions.check: The form shows one tile per service in the fixture's catalogue, in the catalogue's order, laid out in two columns, each tile reading the service's name and its one line.

decisions.decision: While saving, Save greys out and a line under the buttons shows a spinner, what is happening and the seconds counting.
decisions.why: Round 13: started, still alive and failed must look different.
decisions.check: Save is disabled, and a line below the buttons holds a spinner and reads "Checking the login with Salesforce, 6 s".

decisions.decision: A failed save turns the same line red: what failed, that nothing was saved, and what to do; Save is ready again.
decisions.check: The line below the buttons reads "Salesforce refused the client secret. Nothing was saved. Check the secret and save again." in red, and Save is enabled.

decisions.decision: Salesforce's fields are Name, Org, Client id and Client secret (masked). Org is a dropdown of the orgs Bidspoke knows, by name, with the address in a grey line under it, and Another org last. Choosing Another org makes Org a box the new org's address is typed into, and its menu offers "Use <address> as a new org". Who it acts as is read from Salesforce when the login is checked, never typed.
decisions.why: Round 15, and round 25 for an org Bidspoke does not know.
decisions.check: The fields are Name, Org, Client id and Client secret in that order; Client secret is a password field; and no field asks who it acts as. On a known org, Org is a dropdown reading Achieve with achieve.my.salesforce.com in a grey line under it. On an org Bidspoke does not know, Name reads Lendco Salesforce and Org is a box (a combobox, its menu open, no dropdown button) reading lendco.my.salesforce.com, with one option under it reading "Use lendco.my.salesforce.com as a new org".

decisions.decision: Google's fields are Name, then two choice cards, "A company mailbox or drive" (From the company list) and "My own Google account" (Signed in as you); the company card shows a dropdown of the company list.
decisions.check: After the Name field come two choice cards reading A company mailbox or drive with From the company list, and My own Google account with Signed in as you; when the company card is chosen a dropdown reading ops@trypennie.com follows them, and when the own account card is chosen there is none.

decisions.decision: For your own Google account, Google's own white Sign in with Google button, with its logo, replaces Save.
decisions.check: The form's first button is a white button reading Sign in with Google that holds Google's logo, and no button reads Save.

decisions.decision: After a save, the new connection opens in the panel and is chosen in the list, with no message.
decisions.why: Round 18: the connection itself is the proof it saved.
decisions.check: Achieve Salesforce 2 is the chosen list item, the panel is headed Achieve Salesforce 2, and nothing on the page says Saved.

decisions.decision: Reconnect opens a dialog "Reconnect <name>" with the client id kept and a New client secret field, Save and Cancel. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.
decisions.why: Round 19, and round 26 for the title's size.
decisions.check: A dialog titled Reconnect Achieve Salesforce, its title a heading that computes to font-size 20px, holds a Client id field with the kept id, an empty password field New client secret, and the buttons Save and Cancel.

decisions.decision: Replace opens a dialog "Replace <name>" with a Replace with dropdown, the workflows listed and ticked under "In these workflows", "Each ticked workflow gets a new version with <replacement>.", and a red "Replace in <n> workflows" and Cancel. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.
decisions.why: Round 20: some workflows can be left on the old connection. Round 26 for the title's size.
decisions.check: A dialog titled Replace Pennie Salesforce, its title a heading that computes to font-size 20px, holds a Replace with dropdown reading TPL2 Salesforce, In these workflows with each of the connection's 6 workflows ticked, the sentence "Each ticked workflow gets a new version with TPL2 Salesforce.", a red Replace in 6 workflows button and Cancel.

decisions.decision: Removing a connection no workflow uses: Remove is ready, and it opens a dialog "Remove <name>?" saying "Its login is deleted from Bidspoke and cannot be brought back.", with Cancel and a red Remove. Its title is 20px, the size of every dialog's title.
decisions.why: Round 21, and round 26 for the title's size.
decisions.check: On a connection no workflow uses, Remove is enabled and red and its row gives no reason it cannot be removed; on the remove frame a dialog titled Remove Achieve Salesforce 2?, its title a heading that computes to font-size 20px, reads the sentence and holds Cancel and a red Remove.

decisions.decision: When login checks are not answering, a strip at the top says so and gives the time of the last statuses, with Try again; the last known statuses stay shown, Needs attention included.
decisions.check: A strip above the list reads "Login checks are not answering. Statuses are as of 11:52 AM ET." with a Try again button, and the Needs attention group and every status are still shown.

decisions.decision: When the list did not load, one card across the page says so, with Try again, and Add connection is hidden until it loads.
decisions.check: The page holds one card reading "The connections could not be loaded: Bidspoke's server did not answer." with Try again, no connection list, and no Add connection button.

decisions.decision: Blue is for buttons only; links are dark and underlined.
decisions.check: Nothing in the main content outside a button is coloured blue (#1B72BA) in its text or background, and every link is dark (#1D212F) and underlined.

decisions.decision: Red is only for something genuinely wrong, or for the button that destroys.
decisions.check: Red (#B42318) text or background appears only on a problem's status, a failed save's line, and an enabled Remove or Replace in button.

decisions.decision: Every fact once per screen.
decisions.noCode: A review rule for the copy, kept by reading each frame; there is nothing to build for it.

decisions.decision: No line of text ends with a single word on its own line; reword or rebalance it. A rule for all of Bidspoke's copy, made by Dan on 2026-10-20 in these rounds.
decisions.check: No block of text in the main content wraps so that its last line holds a single word.

idioms: The page is drawn at 1120 wide inside a captured copy of the app's chrome; the sidebar and fonts are the app's, not decisions.
Dialogs are drawn over a dimmed copy of the page; the dim is the app's dialog component, not a decision.
The spinner is drawn still; in the app it turns, and the seconds count up.
